agency_full: National Aeronautics and Space Administration / Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory
payload: Mercury orbiter; sunshade-protected (front-side 370 °C, back-side -45 °C); seven instruments including imaging, spectrometers, magnetometer, laser altimeter
credit: © NASA / Johns Hopkins APL — U.S. Government work, public domain. MESSENGER (MErcury Surface, Space ENvironment, GEochemistry, and Ranging) was the first spacecraft to orbit Mercury and the first to map its surface in full. Orbited Mercury 2011-03-18 to 2015-04-30 (~4096 orbits). Discoveries: water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters; previously unknown 'hollows' geological feature; quantified Mercury's iron core (~85 % of the planet's radius — the largest core/planet ratio in the solar system); mapped the planet's magnetic field offset from its geographic centre. Mission ended with a controlled impact onto Mercury's surface 2015-04-30 (no further fuel for orbit maintenance).

events.label: Launch — Delta II 7925H
events.description: Cape Canaveral, 2004-08-03. The first Mercury orbiter — predecessor Mariner 10 (1974) only managed three flybys. MESSENGER (Mercury Surface, Space Environment, Geochemistry, and Ranging) took 6.5 years and six gravity assists to lose the orbital energy needed to capture into Mercury orbit.

events.label: Earth — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 2,348 km on 2005-08-02. First of six gravity assists in the EVVMMM (Earth-Venus-Venus-Mercury-Mercury-Mercury) cruise plan. Each one removes orbital energy, the OPPOSITE of an outer-planet mission's energy gain.

events.label: Venus #1 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 3,000 km on 2006-10-24. Mid-cruise instrument checkout flyby.

events.label: Venus #2 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 338 km on 2007-06-05 — a much deeper pass than #1, removing significant heliocentric velocity.

events.label: Mercury #1 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 200 km on 2008-01-14. First spacecraft to visit Mercury since Mariner 10's third flyby in 1975. Returned new imagery of the hemisphere Mariner 10 never saw.

events.label: Mercury #2 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 200 km on 2008-10-06. Completed mapping of the previously-unobserved hemisphere — by the third flyby >95% of Mercury's surface had imagery for the first time in human history.

events.label: Mercury #3 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 228 km on 2009-09-29. Final pre-orbit flyby — the trajectory was now tuned for Mercury orbital capture 17 months later.

events.label: Mercury orbit insertion
events.description: 2011-03-18. 15-minute main engine burn captured MESSENGER into a highly-elliptical 12-hour Mercury orbit — the first spacecraft to orbit Mercury. Mapped surface composition + topography for 4 years before exhausting fuel and impacting the surface on 2015-04-30 in a planned end-of-mission disposal.
